checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The prose opens on flat, informational atmosphere ('no diesel, no lake, no season,' an ident overlay 'slow enough only the body noticed') that reads as competent worldbuilding exposition rather than seduction; sensory detail throughout (recorder grips, bicycle bearings, checkpoint procedures) serves plot/tracking logic more than lush or strange-beautiful texture, and the horror (Type C reversals, bleed, calibration) arrives quickly via clinical taxonomy ('Type A,' 'Type B,' 'Type C') before the reader has been pulled in by wonder or allure.
checks.Fix: Before cataloguing anomalies and mechanisms, slow down on one fully sensory, covetous image of GLMZ's enhanced life — the specific pleasure of carrier-grade fluency, the beauty of a body that reads a room or a road perfectly — so the wrongness lands as a violation of something the reader was first seduced into wanting.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening beats immediately foreground plot machinery — Amara noting the arcology has no clocks as a deliberate observation for the reader, then diving straight into an interview that exists to reveal Daud's manipulated affect ('Fine. Four times in seven minutes'). There is no unforced commute, transaction, or ordinary moment where the world is simply doing its work before the conspiracy demands attention; the very first paragraphs are already thematically loaded exposition about managed air and surveillance dread.
checks.Fix: Open with a genuinely mundane, plot-agnostic beat — Amara or Seto moving through an ordinary transaction or commute where the city's texture is enjoyed or endured for its own sake — before any hint of the calibration anomaly or investigation surfaces.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Terms like 'CorpoNations,' 'neuretics,' 'Batch 44-C,' 'Zone 5,' 'the Seam,' 'Waxwing overlay,' and 'GLMZ' are dropped in without any in-voice orientation — e.g. 'Second-generation neuretics — you could see it in the old mount scar behind his ear' assumes the reader already knows what neuretics are and does, while 'Waxwing AR glowed along the public edges' and 'the civic AR died in the gap' arrive as bare labels with no grounding gloss for a first-time reader.
checks.Fix: Give the earliest uses of core proprietary terms (neuretics, the Seam, Zone numbering, CorpoNations, Waxwing) one clause of sensory or functional context filtered through the POV's own frame of reference, e.g. 'neuretics — the in-skull hardware everyone her age had gotten used to ignoring' — rather than assuming the reader already carries the worldbuilding.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Multiple acronyms appear with no expansion anywhere on the page: 'GLMZ' is used repeatedly (e.g., 'Every book could be a reader's first GLMZ book' framing aside, but in-text: 'Public GLMZ health data through Infrastructure Authority portals' and 'the smell before rain on the loading dock at GLMZ') with no full term ever glossed; 'AR' appears as 'no Waxwing overlay either — the civic AR died in the gap' with no expansion of 'augmented reality' or in-voice term given first.
checks.Fix: Introduce GLMZ and AR each with an in-voice full-term gloss on their first appearance (e.g., 'the Greater Lakes Metro Zone Authority — GLMZ — health data' and 'the civic augmented-reality overlay, AR, died in the gap') before using the bare acronym thereafter.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: Amara's 'ghost-grip, involuntary' hand curling toward a recorder she no longer holds, and later the small unplanned moment where 'She left the exits where they were, unread, and watched the water instead' — a professional whose whole body is trained to read rooms for danger choosing, once, not to — reveals a person under the function, and she immediately re-armors by not naming or interrogating the moment.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The final beat—Amara's hand finding Seto's, her deciding to 'let the exits where they were, unread'—is a genuine quiet gesture past the plot's business, and it earns its stillness through the Nuru non-event ('She didn't go'). But it slides toward a soft, faintly hopeful resolution ('watched the water instead') rather than landing on unresolved weight; the closing image reads more like relief/connection than cost, and the piece doesn't leave a final line pulling toward 'what happens in this city' so much as toward these two characters' private moment.
checks.Fix: Cut or complicate the tenderness of the final image—end instead on a detail that reasserts the city's ongoing machinery (the fountain's timer, the next Tuesday cohort, the compliant ones still arriving) so the last beat carries cost and scale rather than settling into the couple's relief.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The recurring 'Fine' motif (Daud's flattened affect, Amara's own broadcast-neutral 'Fine,' and the closing single-word 'Fine.' before the fountain scene) works as a complete emotional beat on first read—she notices sources have gone hollow—but only pays off fully once a reader knows the calibration protocol strips weight from memory, retroactively recasting every earlier 'fine' as a diagnostic marker; likewise the exit-counting habit (read in full on first pass as tradecraft/anxiety) becomes poignant in hindsight when she 'left the exits where they were, unread' in the final line, a deliberate inversion that only lands once you've tracked the pattern across the whole story.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The node is a dense, in-media-res thriller chapter that assumes deep familiarity with an entire pre-built mythology (Batch 44-C, the bleed mechanic, the Seam/zone geography, Waxwing AR, Orison's calibration protocol, 847 names, Ciro's razor motif, Doru, Tasmin, the courier trade lexicon) without ever pausing to orient a first-time reader; terms like 'the bleed,' 'recalibration,' and 'Type C' are used as established vocabulary rather than introduced.
checks.Fix: Add brief grounding beats early on—one or two clarifying sentences or a short scene-setting aside—that let a newcomer understand what the bleed is, what Batch 44-C means, and why the 847 names matter before the plot machinery accelerates, without cutting any existing scenes or restructuring the narrative.
